messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Name Removed]

Gender: Male

Age: 71

Admission Date: [Date Removed]

Discharge Date: [Date Removed]

Reason for Admission:

The patient was admitted with general malaise and abnormal findings of computed tomography (CT).

Medical History:

The patient had undergone cystostomy and exchange of the catheter at regular intervals. In addition, he had a history of operation for gastric cancer with lung metastasis.

Medical Findings:

Physical examination was unremarkable. Abnormal findings of complete blood count and laboratory examination included an elevated WBC count and C-reactive protein. On the other hand, fasting blood sugar and hemoglobin A1c were within normal limits. Urinalysis showed combined hematuria and pyuria, and Escherichia coli was detected in urine culture.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

Due to poor condition, the patient underwent construction of the left nephrostomy. After that, remission of the inflammation was achieved, and nephrostomy catheter was also exchanged with cystostomy. Several months after the construction, the patient received left nephrectomy by open surgery. Surgical dissection was very difficult due to fixed mass. The patient received massive transfusions due to uncontrolled bleeding from frequent, extensive adhesions.

Outcome:

Unfortunately, the patient died due to sepsis and cardiovascular failure not long after the surgery.

Follow-up Care:

N/A

Signed by: [Name Removed], M.D.

Date: [Date Removed]

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The picture fits xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis: E. coli urinary infection with high inflammatory markers, an abnormal CT, nephrostomy drainage, then a difficult nephrectomy for a fixed, densely adherent mass. Emphysematous pyelonephritis (N10) is the main alternative, since the normal glucose and HbA1c may have been noted to exclude diabetes; the diagnosis section is withheld, so this is an inference. Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis is a chronic tubulo-interstitial nephritis in chapter N, category N11.

CODE: N11
